scope: Targeted static ELF/source comparison only. No proprietary disassembly/decompilation, module load, hardware test, or binary modification.

r580_proprietary_core.handling: Downloaded and extracted without package scripts; not installed, loaded, modified, redistributed, or relicensed.

r595_open_core.version: 595.104.02, as stated in the source README
r595_open_core.revision_status: The cache directory has no .git metadata; its suffix is not independently verified as a Git commit.

method.targeted_name_search: Exact symbol-name searches covered registerHalModule_GV100, gpuConstructPhysical*, gr*_GV100, subdeviceCtrlCmdKGrInternalStaticGetInfo/Caps (including _IMPL), nvUvmInterface*, GB202/GB203, and GSPCLIENT names. The R580 numeric _nvNNNNNNrm pattern was counted separately.

strong_global_symbol_intersection.rule: Count unique STB_GLOBAL, defined, non-ABS ELF symbols from readelf -W -s; STB_WEAK is excluded. Intersection is exact symbol-name equality between the two ET_REL objects.
strong_global_symbol_intersection.interpretation_limit: The 210 repeated strong global names predict direct-link duplicate-definition conflicts unless symbols are isolated or renamed. This is a name-level link-risk count, not proof of kernel exports, ABI compatibility, equivalent semantics, or runtime interoperability.

symbol_findings.target: R580 GV100 HAL registration, physical construction, GR/FB/FIFO initialization, and GB202/GB203/GSPCLIENT names
symbol_findings.r580_observation: No readable exact target-name matches were found in nm -a. This does not establish that the code paths are absent: 58417 defined symbol names match _nv[0-9]+rm, and sample entries are local functions (readelf: _nv054968rm FUNC LOCAL DEFAULT .text value 0x0 size 5; _nv055133rm FUNC LOCAL DEFAULT .text value 0x10 size 30). The architecture semantics of those numbered symbols were not inferred.
symbol_findings.r595_open_observation: No registerHalModule_GV100, gr*_GV100, or GB202/GB203/GSPCLIENT-named counterpart was found in the proprietary R580 symbol names. See the separate R595 Open findings below; symbol-name absence in R580 is inconclusive.

source: src/nvidia/generated/g_hal_private.h:462-490 defines the GB202/GB203 HAL interface objects and calls registerHalModule(HAL_IMPL_GB202/GB203, ...).
src/nvidia/generated/g_hal_register.h:169-189 declares and invokes the GB20x registrations.
symbol_findings.interpretation: The registration symbols are present in this R595 Open object. The halIface objects are local, not global exports. No GV100 registration counterpart was found in the Open source search.

The object contains named GV100 FIFO, GMMU and memory-system helpers that are concrete reuse candidates. Their presence does not establish that the complete GV100 initialization path or a functional Volta driver exists.
These named helpers exist in the R595 Open core object. They do not prove that R580 proprietary contains equivalent code under a usable interface or that any GSP path is suitable for GV100.

symbol_findings.target: Physical construction and GR dispatch methods
r595_open_source: src/nvidia/generated/g_gpu_nvoc.h:1752-1757 and :4856 implement generic gpuConstructPhysical as static inline code; src/nvidia/src/kernel/gpu/gpu.c:676 calls it. It is not a standalone named object symbol and is not GV100-specific.

src/nvidia/generated/g_subdevice_nvoc.h:2359 and :2369 declare subdeviceCtrlCmdKGrInternalStaticGetInfo_IMPL and ...GetCaps_IMPL; g_subdevice_nvoc.c:2113 and :2233 contain dispatch-table pointer references. Neither exact name appears in nm -a for the compared R595 nv-kernel.o object. The reason (build configuration, conditional inclusion, or component boundary) is not established by these observations.
symbol_findings.architecture_tree: The R595 source tree has no src/nvidia/src/kernel/gpu/gr/arch/volta directory. It does have fifo/arch/volta, mem_mgr/arch/volta and mem_sys/arch/volta. GR directories include Maxwell, Pascal, Turing, Ampere and Blackwell.
symbol_findings.interpretation: This is evidence of partial reusable Volta support, not an open GV100 GR backend in this source release. The generated generic constructor and GR control names do not replace architecture-specific GR registration and implementation.

symbol_findings.observation: No nvUvmInterface* symbol name was found in either compared nv-kernel core object. This comparison does not include the separate nvidia-uvm kernel component or establish UVM availability.

source_observations.observation: The R580 wrapper describes nv-kernel.o_binary as the core binary component shared across UNIX platforms and links it through an nv-kernel.o symlink into nvidia.ko. Thus this symbol comparison covers the opaque core object, not the complete Linux module interface.

rm_is_supported_pci_device is a named R580 global function (value 0xd67790, size 317). The PCI probe passes PCI base class, subclass, vendor, device, subsystem vendor/device and NV_FALSE before enabling/probing the device; the VGA/3D enumeration passes the corresponding fields with NV_TRUE. After the probe copies the PCI identifiers into nv_state, rm_is_supported_device(sp,nv) is called (value 0xd67470, size 797); failure exits before rm_init_private_state and the 'Wire RM HAL' step.

The R580 wrapper explicitly requires Open kernel modules for a narrowly defined self-hosted-Hopper/Blackwell PCI-ID set (GH100 0x2340-0x237f; GB100 0x2940-0x297f; GB110 0x31c0-0x31ff or 0x31a1). This special-case check is not evidence of general RTX 5090/5080 support in the proprietary branch.

The source README identifies version 595.104.02, requires matching GSP firmware and user-space components, and states Open kernel modules are usable on Turing or later. Volta is outside that documented support floor despite the GV100 helper symbols and Volta subdirectories.

The package says individual files are MIT-licensed except where noted; a linked Linux kernel module is dual licensed MIT/GPLv2. Check file-level notices before reusing particular files. This does not grant rights to redistribute the proprietary R580 object.

decision_limits: No symbol-name match in the R580 proprietary object is not evidence that the corresponding machine-code path is absent: its internal implementation names are largely numeric _nvNNNNNNrm names, whose semantics were not mapped.
A defined ELF symbol is not necessarily a kernel-exported symbol, stable interface, reachable dispatch entry, or implementation compatible with the other object.
The 210 matching global names predict an un-namespaced direct-link collision risk; no combined link was attempted in this bounded audit.
No object-level comparison proves device initialization, CUDA execution, UVM, P2P, stability, or performance on hardware.
The R595 compiled object is identified by its SHA256 and cache path; its full build flags and Git revision are unavailable.

next_discriminating_experiments.question: Does the R580 RM policy accept each actual PCI ID, and at which gate does a device fail?
next_discriminating_experiments.experiment: On a disposable canary, log the arguments and return values of rm_is_supported_pci_device and rm_is_supported_device at the nv-pci.c call sites before rm_init_private_state, separately for verified V100 and Blackwell PCI devices. A false early gate distinguishes PCI allow-list policy from later RM/HAL initialization failure. Do not infer these returns from the symbol table.

next_discriminating_experiments.question: Can R580 and R595 core objects be directly linked together?
next_discriminating_experiments.experiment: In a scratch directory only, run a relocatable link of copies with ld -r and capture the first duplicate-definition diagnostics. The 210-name overlap predicts failure without namespace isolation/renaming; the link result is still not an ABI or runtime test.
